text: Hi, I am Ankur Budhbul, and this video is about why AI pipelines silently degrade. In traditional software, a function that adds two numbers today will still add them tomorrow. But when you wrap an application around a large language model, a change in model version, a rewarded system prompt, or a shift in upstream data can break your downstream architecture without anyone touching your code. You cannot test what a model will say. You can test everything you built around it, and you can make the repository refuse code that breaks it. That is the whole of continuous integration for AI. Testing AI is fundamentally different from testing standard code. You cannot

Assert that a model's output will precisely match a hardcoded string. Instead, you test the deterministic guardrails that surround it. Continuous integration for AI means continuously testing your parsers, your normalizers, and your fail-safes against a suite of known adversarial inputs. This is where a continuous integration pipeline, something like GitHub Actions, stops being a nicety. A CI pipeline is an automated robot living in your repository. Every time an engineer tries to update the system, it rebuilds the application in a vacuum and fires malicious data at it before a human ever sees the change. So, let's watch what happens when someone deletes a security check and tries to merge it anyway. This

Is the moment the whole pipeline is for. If a developer accidentally removes a security rejects or a new model update starts slipping past the evaluation logic, the pipeline catches it in isolation. It locks the repository and stops the compromised code from reaching production. That is the difference between hoping your guardrails held and knowing they did. So, never assume your guardrails will survive the next commit. Build an automated integration pipeline that aggressively attacks your own system on every update, and make a failing attack block the merge. And here is the prompt worth running before you trust any of it. Hand a model your test suite and ask which of your guardrails

It could break without a single test going red. The gap between what you test and what you rely on is where the next regression is already living. Your model will change under you. Your tests are the only thing that notices. Ankur Budge Ball for Humanitarians AI.
